definition: Performance assessment is a way of judging how well an organization or system is doing by using selected standards or outcomes. In this source, it refers to appraisal systems that rate government performance using economic results, environmental results, or a combination of both, which can shape later behavior and its social effects.

reasons: The first sentence (“Performance assessment is a way of judging how well an organization or system is doing by using selected standards or outcomes”) is a general definition not explicitly supported by the provided packet text.

While the packet discusses “economic performance assessment,” “environmental assessment system,” and a “multidimensional appraisal system” used to evaluate government competition in relation to ecological welfare performance, the definition’s framing is broader than what the packet states (e.g., it generalizes beyond the government/ecological-welfare context to “organization or system” and “selected standards or outcomes”).

The definition claims these assessments “can shape later behavior and its social effects”; the packet supports effects on “ecological welfare performance” over subsequent periods (current and next four years / long term), but it does not clearly support the specific wording about “behavior and its social effects” as such.
